# easypanel-mcp-server

> MCP Server for full Easypanel control via Claude Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop.

easypanel-mcp-server is a Model Context Protocol server that exposes 57 tools for managing Easypanel — a modern Docker-based server control panel. Use it to deploy apps, manage services, configure env vars, read runtime logs, exec commands inside containers, manage domains, databases, volumes and ports, set resource limits, run Docker maintenance, and monitor infrastructure directly from Claude Code or Cursor — plus an `easypanel_raw` escape hatch reaching any of Easypanel's ~375 API operations. v3.x speaks all three Easypanel API generations (tRPC on panels ≤ 2.30, the RPC layer of 2.31–2.32, and the public API of 2.33+) with automatic detection.

## Available tools (57)

- `list_projects`: List all Easypanel projects with their services and status
- `get_project`: Get full details of a project including all services
- `create_project`: Create a new project
- `delete_project`: Permanently delete a project and all its services — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `inspect_service`: Get complete service config: source, env vars, deploy settings, mounts, ports, resources. Routes by service type (app, compose, databases). Use BEFORE any update to preserve current state.
- `create_service`: Create a new app service in a project
- `rename_service`: Rename or move a service — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `destroy_service`: Permanently destroy a service — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `deploy_service`: Trigger a deploy with the current source configuration
- `start_service`: Start a stopped service
- `stop_service`: Stop a service in production — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO". Works for app and (on Easypanel 2.33+) compose services
- `restart_service`: Restart a service
- `get_service_error`: Get the last recorded error from a service — use for debugging
- `get_service_notes`: Read notes saved on a service
- `set_service_notes`: Save notes on a service (markdown supported)
- `set_service_resources`: Set CPU/memory limits and reservations (memory in MB, CPU in cores). Partial updates merge with current values.
- `set_source_github`: Configure GitHub as the deploy source (owner, repo, branch, path)
- `set_source_image`: Configure a Docker image as the deploy source
- `enable_github_deploy`: Enable auto-deploy on every GitHub push
- `disable_github_deploy`: Disable GitHub auto-deploy
- `list_actions`: List running or recent deploy/build jobs (filterable by projectName/serviceName/type) — use to track deploy progress
- `get_action`: Get details and logs of a specific action by ID
- `get_env_vars`: List all environment variables. Sensitive values (KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD) are masked by default. Use include_values: true to reveal.
- `set_env_var`: Add or update ONE env var safely — reads current state before writing, never wipes other vars
- `delete_env_var`: Remove ONE env var — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `get_service_logs`: Get live container runtime logs via WebSocket (last N lines, max 500)
- `get_build_logs`: Get the full build/deploy log of the service's latest deployment
- `get_exposed_ports`: List a service's host-published ports
- `get_system_stats`: Get server metrics: CPU, memory, disk, network, uptime
- `list_domains`: List all domains configured for a service
- `add_domain`: Add a custom domain with automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt
- `remove_domain`: Remove a domain — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `set_primary_domain`: Set the primary domain for a service
- `create_database`: Create a Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB or Redis service
- `inspect_database`: Get database details including credentials and connection string
- `destroy_database`: Permanently destroy a database and all its data — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `get_docker_stats`: Get Docker task state per service — running replicas (actual) vs desired. For CPU/memory of one service use get_service_stats
- `get_storage_stats`: Get server storage usage
- `get_service_stats`: Get CPU, memory and network metrics for a specific service container
- `list_containers`: List a service's running Docker containers (ID, image, command, status, ports)
- `exec_in_container`: Run a shell command inside a service's container and return its output — for runtime debugging
- `get_docker_events`: Capture real-time Docker events during a short window (start/stop/kill/die/exec/health)
- `list_mounts`: List a service's volumes/mounts (named volumes and bind mounts)
- `create_mount`: Add a named volume or bind mount to a service. Sensitive host paths (/, /etc, docker.sock) require confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `list_ports`: List a service's host port mappings (published → target, protocol)
- `create_port`: Publish a host port mapping. Privileged ports (< 1024) require confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `create_compose`: Create a Docker Compose service
- `inspect_compose`: Get a Compose service's configuration
- `deploy_compose`: Deploy (docker compose up) a Compose service
- `cleanup_docker_images`: Remove unused Docker images server-wide to free space
- `prune_docker`: Run a global "docker system prune" (containers, networks, build cache, unused images) — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `list_users`: List panel users (sensitive fields — apiToken, 2FA secret, password — are redacted)
- `list_certificates`: List SSL/TLS certificates managed by Easypanel
- `list_nodes`: List Docker Swarm cluster nodes (local node only on single-server setups)
- `restart_panel`: Restart Easypanel itself — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `reboot_server`: Reboot the entire host server — requires confirm: "CONFIRMO"
- `easypanel_raw`: Call any Easypanel API operation directly (~375). On panels 2.33+ use the flat public name (`listCertificates`); the old dot notation (`certificates.listCertificates`) is still accepted and translated. Reads by default; writes require isMutation: true and confirm: "CONFIRMO". The old tool name `trpc_raw` still routes for backward compatibility

## Quick start

Add to your `.mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "easypanel-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "easypanel-mcp-server"],
      "env": {
        "EASYPANEL_URL": "https://your-panel.example.com",
        "EASYPANEL_TOKEN": "your-api-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Required environment variables

- `EASYPANEL_URL` (required): Your Easypanel panel URL without trailing slash
- `EASYPANEL_TOKEN` (required): API token — generate at Easypanel → Settings → API → Generate Token
- `MCP_ACCESS_MODE` (optional): set to `readonly` to block all writes (curated tools and easypanel_raw); reads stay available
- `EASYPANEL_RAW_DISABLED` (optional): set to `1` to disable the easypanel_raw escape hatch entirely
- `EASYPANEL_API_FLAVOR` (optional): force the panel API generation instead of auto-detecting — `trpc` (Easypanel ≤ 2.30), `rpc` (2.31–2.32) or `public` (≥ 2.33). Remove a stale `rpc` pin from v2, or a 2.33 panel stays on the internal API

## Safety features

Every response that touches a project/service starts with a context banner:
```
[Contexto ativo: projeto="my-project" | serviço="my-api"]
```

Destructive actions (delete, destroy, stop, prune, reboot) return `status: "BLOQUEADO"` unless `confirm: "CONFIRMO"` is passed explicitly. Env var updates use read-modify-write to never accidentally wipe existing variables. `list_users` redacts apiToken/2FA secret/password. Read-only mode (`MCP_ACCESS_MODE=readonly`) blocks all writes at the source.

## Known limitations

- WordPress/Box service types have no dedicated tools — reach them via `easypanel_raw` (`inspectWordPressService`, `createBoxService`)
- `easypanel_raw` reads bypass read-only mode and can return secrets — use `EASYPANEL_RAW_DISABLED=1` in untrusted environments
- `list_nodes` returns the local node only on single-server setups (no Swarm cluster)
- Docker events are real-time only (no history) — an idle server may return an empty window
